final_answer:
A stack is a data structure that follows the LIFO (Last In, First Out) principle, where the last element added is the first one to be removed. A queue follows the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle, where the first element added is the first one to be removed.

A real-world example of a stack is a browser history. When you navigate back, the most recent page is the one that gets closed first. A real-world example of a queue is a printer queue. Print jobs are processed in the order they were received, with the first job being printed first.
